title: Fatwa RAG - common corpus record
description: Every source, bulk dataset or scraped site, collapses into this one shape. data/corpus.json is a JSON array of these objects. To add a scraped source: (1) register it in SOURCE_META in config.py, (2) write an adapter in ingest.py that builds records through make_doc(), (3) add it to ADAPTERS. Nothing downstream changes. make_doc() computes id, native_id, content_hash, provenance and retrieved_at for you, so an adapter only supplies title, question, answer, categories and url. validate_docs() then fails the ingest loudly if any field is missing or out of vocabulary.

id.description: Globally unique, always '<source>:<native_id>'. Asserted unique at ingest.

source.description: Short machine key. Must exist in SOURCE_META in config.py.

native_id.description: The source's own identifier, stored separately from `id` so a scraper can resume, diff or re-fetch a page without string-splitting. Always a string, even when the site uses integers.

content_hash.description: SHA1 (first 16 hex chars) of case- and whitespace-normalised title+question+answer. THE field that makes re-scraping safe: same hash means the page is unchanged so skip it; a changed hash means the fatwa was edited; the same hash under two different ids means the same fatwa republished on two sites, which happens constantly between Hanafi darul-iftas. Computed by make_doc, never supplied.

source_label.description: Human-readable name shown on the card badge.

source_url.description: Site root, for attribution. Distinct from `url`, which points at this one fatwa.

record_type.description: THE ONLY REAL BRANCH IN THE SYSTEM. 'single_source' = one scholar or site answering, read `answer`. 'multi_school' = several schools compared inside one record, read `positions`. Retrieval, storage and badging are otherwise identical.

orientation.description: Fixed vocabulary, mirrored in config.ORIENTATIONS. Shown on every card - we never present a single-madhhab source as neutral. Enumerated rather than free text so a scraper cannot silently split one badge into 'Salafi' / 'salafi' / 'Salafi-leaning'. A new site means adding its orientation to config.ORIENTATIONS first.

madhhab.description: Set when a single_source record has a known school. Null for multi_school records, which use `positions`, and for sources with no declared school.

scholar.description: Answering scholar or mufti where known. Defaults from SOURCE_META.

url.description: Canonical link to THIS fatwa. Every rendered card links here - no uncited claim is displayed.

license.description: Carried per record so mixed-licence corpora stay auditable.

retrieved_at.description: ISO date WE snapshotted the source. Fatwa sites change; this dates our copy of the claim.

date_published.description: ISO date the SOURCE published the fatwa, where the site exposes it. Null for both bulk datasets. Worth capturing when scraping: a 2003 ruling on banking and a 2023 one are different evidence.

question.description: The questioner's text, boilerplate prefixes stripped.

answer.description: single_source: the full fatwa body, at least MIN_ANSWER_CHARS long. multi_school: the summary statement across schools.

question_arabic.description: Original-language question, where the English is a translation. Null when the source is natively English.

answer_arabic.description: Original-language anchor text. For FiqhQA this is the authoritative field - the per-school English is a structured summary of it.

categories.description: ALWAYS a list, never a string. IslamQA cross-lists one fatwa under several topics; deduping by URL merges those labels rather than discarding them. Single-topic sources get a one-element list. Also the stratification key for sampling.

positions.description: multi_school only; null otherwise, and validation rejects a single_source record that carries them. Exactly four entries in SCHOOL_KEYS order, INCLUDING schools with no recorded opinion, so absence is explicit rather than silent.

has_opinion.description: False where the source states the school has no recorded view. Render as 'no recorded position', never as a ruling.

designRules.oneBranch: record_type is the only thing any consumer switches on. single_source reads `answer`; multi_school reads `positions`. Retrieval, badging and storage are identical either way.
designRules.noSourceSpecificFields: Every field means the same thing for every source, or it does not belong. This is what makes the corpus mergeable across four sources today and a fifth tomorrow without touching embed.py, search.py or app.py. WHAT THIS RULE REMOVED: FiqhQA's `Agreement` column (Agreement/Disagreement). It was meaningful for 121 records and null for the other ~3,900 - a per-source annotation wearing a common-schema costume. It still exists in data/raw/fiqhqa.parquet and eval.py joins it back by native_id when scoring the comparison layer, so nothing was lost except the pollution.
designRules.derivedNotStored: Retrieval text is computed, never persisted - see derivedFields. Storing it doubled the corpus file. A scraped adapter cannot get these wrong because it never supplies them.
designRules.controlledVocabularies: orientation and madhhab are enums, not free text, so a scraper cannot silently split one UI badge into three spellings.
designRules.validationAtIngest: schema.py validate_docs() runs at the end of every ingest AND every scrape, and fails the run naming the offending id and field. A missing url breaks the build, not the demo.

derivedFields.description: NOT stored in corpus.json. Computed as properties on Doc (schema.py) because they are pure functions of the content - persisting them doubled the file, bm25_text alone being 46% of it. A scraped adapter never supplies these, so it cannot get them wrong.
derivedFields.embed_text: title + question. Deliberately excludes the answer: user queries are questions, and question-to-question similarity is far stronger than question-to-answer.
derivedFields.bm25_text: title + question + answer + every stated school position. Carries the substance so rare domain terms - riba, masah, mudarabah, istihada - stay findable by keyword, which embeddings handle poorly.
derivedFields.llm_context: answer truncated to MAX_ANSWER_CHARS_FOR_LLM at a word boundary.

sampling.description: IslamQA is 15,296 unique fatwas after cleaning - more than a one-day demo needs, and it would dominate every other source in the corpus. config.ISLAMQA_SAMPLE_FRAC takes a stratified 10%: proportional within each of the 266 topics with a floor of one, seeded at SAMPLE_SEED=42. Stratifying rather than sampling at random keeps the topic mix identical to the full corpus and guarantees no topic disappears. Set ISLAMQA_SAMPLE_FRAC=1.0, or run `python ingest.py --full`, to build the whole thing; nothing else changes.
sampling.pins: Stratification protects topic coverage but is blind to what a specific demo query needs. There is exactly ONE bitcoin fatwa in all 15,296, so a 10% sample dropped it. config.SAMPLE_PINS is a list of regexes; any fatwa whose text matches is kept regardless of the sample, currently rescuing 58 docs on finance terms. Add a term whenever a demo query turns out to have thin coverage.
sampling.balance: For the SCRAPED sources the goal is the opposite of preserving the mix - the mix is the bias. islamqa.org holds 91,580 Hanafi URLs against 182 Hanbali, so proportional sampling would rebuild exactly what we are correcting. scrape.py's balanced_quota() fills the smallest madhhab pools to exhaustion first and splits the remainder evenly, so Hanbali and Maliki come in whole and Hanafi/Shafi'i are sampled down to meet them.

examples.question: islamqa.org spans ~40 darul-iftas across all four madhhabs, and the URL path carries both (/maliki/binbayyah/271036/). Unlike every other source its orientation varies row by row, so make_doc takes an orientation override for exactly this case.

sources.description: Three sources, one shape. The corpus was 93% IslamQA.info (Salafi); the two scrapes exist to correct that.
sources.islamqa: kingkaung/english_islamqainfo on HuggingFace. 19,052 rows -> 15,296 unique -> ~1,589 after a stratified 10% sample plus pins. Salafi. CC-BY-NC-4.0.
sources.fiqhqa: REMOVED. MBZUAI/FiqhQA, english config, 121 multi_school rows - the former four-school comparison layer. Dropped because all 121 shared ONE url (the HuggingFace dataset page), so a card's source link led to a download rather than to a fatwa, and none named a scholar. A card reading 'the Hanafi school holds X' with nothing behind it a reader can open is an authority this tool is not entitled to claim. The multi_school record_type is kept above as vocabulary for a future source that CAN cite itself per school; nothing emits it today, and ingest.py and search.py both fail loudly if one appears.
sources.islamqaorg: SCRAPED from islamqa.org. WordPress; wp-json is 401 so scrape.py walks sitemap.xml -> 98,637 URLs. An aggregator over ~40 darul-iftas with madhhab AND institution in the URL path, giving all four Sunni schools labelled per record. Sampled BALANCED not proportional (see sampling.balance).
sources.askimam: SCRAPED from askimam.org. React SPA over a Django REST API at askimam.org:8000; list /api/v1/fatwas/fatwas/?page=N (24,865 total), detail /api/v1/fatwas/fatwas/<id>/. Uniformly Hanafi, Mufti Ebrahim Desai. Pages sampled evenly across the full range so the corpus spans the 2000s-2020s rather than only recent fatwas.
sources.note: islamqa.org republishes askimam under /hanafi/askimam/ (20,386 URLs). Those are skipped there since askimam.org is scraped directly; content_hash would catch any that slip through.
